Final analysis · Paris Airbnb · July–August comparison

Pricing the Games

Are higher nightly prices associated with lower occupancy, and did the price–occupancy relationship differ in July–August 2024 from the same months in 2023?
For hosts considering major-event pricing; these results describe associations and do not identify an optimal price.

Presentation-ready wording

Across the full study sample, mean recorded gross revenue per listing-month was €2,630.81 in 2023 and €2,328.13 in 2024, a change of -€302.68 (-11.5%); mean gross revenue per calendar night was €84.86 versus €75.10 (8,552 listing-months in 2023; 12,620 in 2024). These are observational comparisons of recorded gross revenue, not profit or evidence that price changes caused revenue to change. For LA 2028 hosts, the comparison highlights that higher nightly prices alone do not guarantee higher gross receipts; costs, availability, booking timing, and local demand matter, and Paris does not identify an optimal LA price. Among 2,407 listings observed in all four months, mean recorded gross revenue per listing-month was €3,509.28 in 2023 and €2,888.75 in 2024, a change of -€620.53 (-17.7%); mean gross revenue per calendar night was €113.20 versus €93.19 after averaging July and August within each listing-year. These are observational comparisons of recorded gross revenue, not profit or evidence that price changes caused revenue to change. For LA 2028 hosts, the comparison highlights that higher nightly prices alone do not guarantee higher gross receipts; costs, availability, booking timing, and local demand matter, and Paris does not identify an optimal LA price.

Recorded gross revenue is not profit. These are observational comparisons: they do not show that price changes caused revenue changes and do not identify an optimal LA price.

Revenue field assumption

All study rows report EUR, but `revenue` and `native_revenue` differ (median ratio 1.079). The analysis uses `native_revenue` as EUR, consistently with the `native_avg_daily_rate` assumption. The exact dataset's field-level documentation is incomplete, so this is an explicit assumption; see `final_analysis/revenue_method_notes.md`.

What the results mean

Observed estimates, separated from theory-based expectations.

Observed findings

  • The unadjusted and entire-home-adjusted price slopes are small and statistically uncertain. Their confidence intervals include zero.
  • In Model 3, neither year’s price slope nor the difference between them is statistically clear at the 5% level. The data do not show a reliable change in the price relationship between these periods.
  • Mean occupancy is lower and mean price is higher in the 2024 sample, but that period contrast alone does not establish that price changes caused occupancy to change.
  • For hosts, these estimates do not give an exact best price for Paris or LA. Listing quality, location, timing, availability, and demand could also shape the observed association.

Competing expectations

  • A ticket-driven demand surge and fewer substitutes could make guests less price-sensitive in 2024, weakening a negative price slope.
  • A surge in supply or overpricing against expected demand could strengthen a negative price slope as some listings remain unbooked.
  • These are theory-based competing predictions, not preregistered expectations. The main interaction estimate does not clearly distinguish them.

Sensitivity and measurement notes

The full valid sample remains the primary analysis.

Price field and currency assumption

Every selected row reports currency EUR, but avg_daily_rate and native_avg_daily_rate differ. The analysis uses native_avg_daily_rate as EUR/night, based on its native-currency name and the EUR field. The exact Kaggle file does not document why the fields differ, so this is an explicit assumption. Both values are preserved in the cleaned CSV. The corrected period mean prices are €185.99 (2023) and €257.51 (2024); earlier slides used the other field.

Highest-price sensitivity

Dropping the top 1% (212 observations; prices above about €1,090.58) changes the estimated slope difference to -0.925 pp (p=0.039; 95% CI [-1.802, -0.048]). This negative difference is statistically detectable in that sensitivity but not the full sample; the inference is sensitive to the highest prices.

Top-1% slopes: 2023 +1.753 pp; 2024 +0.828 pp.

Other data choices

The selected sample has 8,801 zero-occupancy rows, retained. `active` was not used to exclude rows because some inactive records have positive occupancy and some active records have zero occupancy. Bedrooms was omitted: 2,814 values are missing and some are unusually large. Entire-home is the common control, plausibly related to both price and demand.

For listings present in all four months, the slope difference is +0.151 pp (p=0.709), consistent with the full-sample inference.

Important limitations

Monthly records combine dates outside the Olympic Games and cannot isolate event days. The year samples differ in size and listing composition. Location, property quality, amenities, timing, minimum stays, and availability may influence both price and occupancy. For example, better locations or higher-quality homes may charge more and attract more bookings, pushing the estimated price association upward (less negative) relative to a causal effect. Listing-clustered errors account for repeated observations, not confounding.

The downloaded Kaggle dataset page provides no readable field-level documentation in this review. An analogous past-calendar schema defines a native rate as an average daily rate in native currency; the applied EUR interpretation is therefore an assumption based on that convention and the sample currency column.
